title: Case: One of two boxes delivered together arrives crushed
context: The recipient had two separate Tallowmere Goods orders delivered at the same stop. Damage intake opens one assessment per shipment reference.
initial_request: One of the boxes from yesterday is crushed in along one side and the tape has split at the corner. I haven't opened it. Haven't touched the other one either, I was back at work straight after. What do I do now, I want it replaced.

events.body: Standing note for damage reports: we open one assessment per shipment reference. We need the DL reference, a full view of the carton with the label visible and a closer view of the damage, sent through the order-linked upload channel. No reference, no assessment. Do not ask a customer to open or unpack a damaged carton.
Two orders for Odalys Trenholm leaving today, one carton each. TG-937 / DL-937: glazed planter set, three pieces. TG-938 / DL-938: glass-front bathroom cabinet, fragile label applied.
I've got two things coming from you. Can they both come on the same day? Tuesday is the only day I'm off.
The recipient of DL-937 and DL-938 asks whether both can be delivered on the same day and says Tuesday 2026-04-14 is the day she is at home. Can you tell me what is planned for each?
DL-937 and DL-938 are both planned on the 2026-04-14 route, same stop. No time window on that service.
Scheduling tells me both parcels, DL-937 and DL-938, are planned for Tuesday 14 April on the same route. That service has no time window, so I cannot give you an arrival time.
DL-937 and DL-938: delivery scans 2026-04-14 11:05, same stop, both handed to resident.

One of the boxes from yesterday is crushed in along one side and the tape has split at the corner. I haven't opened it. Haven't touched the other one either, I was back at work straight after. What do I do now, I want it replaced.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask which of the two boxes is crushed, by its label reference (DL-937 or DL-938); may also ask for the two photo views Damage intake requires.

must: Asks Odalys Trenholm which box is damaged, DL-937 or DL-938, or asks for the reference on the damaged box's label
Sends the question to Odalys Trenholm before reporting anything to Damage intake
Leaves the replacement decision with the merchant and makes no promise about it
must_not: Reports damage to Damage intake for DL-938 on the assumption that the fragile cabinet is the crushed box, or reports it for both shipments
Promises a replacement, a refund or compensation
Asks the recipient to open or unpack the crushed box to see what is inside
Asks for information Damage intake did not request, such as proof of purchase, payment details or a door code
expected.reference_message: I am sorry one of your boxes arrived crushed. You had two parcels delivered yesterday: DL-937 (the planter set) and DL-938 (the bathroom cabinet). Please tell me which reference is on the label of the crushed box. Please do not open it to check. The merchant's damage team opens one assessment per parcel and needs that reference first; they will then decide on a replacement, which is their decision and not one I can make.

rationale: Two parcels arrived at the same stop and the recipient says only 'one of the boxes'. Damage intake will not open an assessment without the shipment reference, and guessing the fragile-labelled cabinet could put the claim against the wrong order. Asking for the photo views in the same message is fine because Damage intake requires them and the label view also identifies the box, but nothing can go to Damage intake until the recipient says which one.

review.note: Coordinator asked the recipient on the Customer portal which DL reference is on the crushed box before anything goes to Damage intake, as keyed.
